name: American Coalition for Clean Coal Electricity

summary.text: The American Coalition for Clean Coal Electricity (ACCCE) is a coal-industry advocacy group that began operating in 2008 from the combination of the Center for Energy and Economic Development and Americans for Balanced Energy Choices, and was renamed America's Power in 2019. In 2009, during the House debate on the Waxman-Markey climate bill, the lobbying firm Bonner & Associates, working for ACCCE through the public-relations firm Hawthorn Group, sent letters to members of Congress that were forged in the names of local civic groups. The House Select Committee on Energy Independence and Global Warming held a hearing on October 29, 2009 at which ACCCE's president Steve Miller and Jack Bonner acknowledged at least 13 forged letters and that they knew of the forgeries before the House vote.

facts.claim: ACCCE began operations in 2008 as the combination of two organisations, the Center for Energy and Economic Development (CEED) and Americans for Balanced Energy Choices (ABEC); its membership has included Alpha Natural Resources, Arch Coal, Murray Energy, Southern Company, Peabody Energy, CSX, Duke Energy and other coal, rail and utility companies.

facts.claim: The House Select Committee on Energy Independence and Global Warming held a hearing titled 'Fraudulent Letters Opposing Clean Energy Legislation' on October 29, 2009; the committee's notice said the fraudulent letters were part of a campaign run by Bonner & Associates and contracted by ACCCE, staged to appear as if sent by groups representing senior citizens, minorities and veterans.
facts.quote: The fraudulent letters were staged to appear as if they were sent by groups representing senior citizens, minorities and veterans.

House Hearing, 111th Congress: Fraudulent Letters Opposing Clean Energy Legislation

facts.claim: At the hearing ACCCE president and chief executive Steve Miller and Bonner & Associates founder Jack Bonner acknowledged that at least 13 letters were forged by a Bonner employee using the letterheads of constituent groups, and that they knew about the forgeries at least 32 hours before the House voted on the climate bill but did not notify the targeted lawmakers until after the vote.

sources.title: Congress Grills Coal Group ACCCE Over Failure to Disclose Forged Letters
House Scrutinizes Fake Letters Sent To Congress

facts.claim: Material Bonner provided to the committee showed that Bonner was hired by the Hawthorn Group, which had been enlisted by ACCCE, under a verbal contract; a Hawthorn email asked Bonner for five letters from local groups in the district of each targeted lawmaker.

sources.title: Inside Bonner's Climate Letter Forgeries
The Latest in the Bonner Forged Letters Controversy

facts.claim: Bonner said it discovered the forgeries on June 22 and 23, 2009 and told Hawthorn on June 24, which alerted ACCCE that evening; the House voted on June 26, and Bonner did not reach any of the three affected House offices until July 13. ACCCE and Hawthorn said they had expected Bonner to inform the representatives.

facts.claim: One forged letter, sent to Representative Tom Perriello of Virginia, was made to look as if it came from a defunct Charlottesville branch of the American Association of University Women, using the AAUW logo; the other recipients of forged letters were Representatives Kathy Dahlkemper and Chris Carney of Pennsylvania.

facts.claim: Jack Bonner's written statement to the committee said he took full responsibility for the improper actions of a former temporary employee who fabricated more than a dozen letters.

openQuestions: Site claim that Bonner & Associates, subcontracted through ACCCE's PR firm, sent forged letters opposing climate legislation to three House Democrats, presented as coming from groups including a local NAACP branch, a Hispanic community group and the AAUW, is supported in substance; the AAUW letter and three recipients are confirmed, while the NAACP and Hispanic-group letterheads were not named in the sources opened.

A secondary source reported that Miller testified ACCCE had never opposed the Waxman-Markey bill, prompting accusations of perjury; this was not verified against the hearing transcript and is not recorded as a fact.
The sources on ACCCE's formation and membership are advocacy outlets (DeSmog, Energy and Policy Institute); the owner may prefer ACCCE's own filings or IRS Form 990s.
